plan: This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: I exit at my bid, and if I win, I pay the second-highest bid. Bidding my true value ($30) is a weakly dominant strategy - if I bid higher, I risk paying more than my value; if I bid lower, I risk losing auctions I'd profit from. Since values are independently drawn and this is a one-shot game, truthful bidding maximizes my expected profit.

This auction structure (winner pays the second-highest sealed bid) is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value, as this ensures I win whenever the price is below my value (profitable) and lose when it's above (avoiding losses), without any incentive to shade the bid up or down. My value is $7, so I will bid $7.

Since the auction mechanism results in the winner paying the second-highest bid (like a second-price auction), bidding my true value is the weakly dominant strategy. Bidding exactly $36 ensures I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids and pay a fair price based on the second-highest bid, maximizing expected profit without risking overpaying or losing profitable opportunities.
